name: Forbidden City: Hall of Supreme Harmony
_about: THE FORBIDDEN CITY's three great halls (1420; the Taihe Dian 1695): the I-shaped white marble terrace in its three tiers, its balustrades, dragon spouts, stairs and imperial ways; the Hall of Supreme Harmony, double-eaved under the true hip (`pent` + `hip`, ten beasts on each hip), brackets under both eaves, 72 red columns, a gallery behind the south front, the throne room; the Halls of Central and Preserving Harmony behind it (`chinese-hall`). Generated by tools/archgen/forbidden_city.py -- edit the script for arithmetic changes. South is +z.

lower tier._about: the terrace's three tiers of white marble, I-shaped: 8.13m in all

lower stairs._about: to the south and north a flight either side of the imperial way; two more flanking on the south; east and west one

lower imperial way._about: the carved slab up the middle (the emperor alone was carried over it): dragons in the clouds, a wedge from tier to tier

panels 1._about: each tier's balustrade: a carved panel to every bay

dragon spouts._about: the dragon heads that spout the terrace's rain, one under each post

hall plinth._about: the hall's low plinth on the top tier

eave columns._about: 72 red columns on the 12 x 6 grid: the outer ring carries the lower eave...

clerestory columns._about: ...the next ring runs up through the lower roof to carry the upper...

gold columns._about: ...and the six about the throne are gilded, with dragons coiling up them

door wall._about: the south front: a gallery one bay deep behind the eave columns, then the door wall -- five bays of lattice doors in the middle, windows on a low wall either side

back wall._about: the other three sides are solid red walls, a door in the back

ceiling._about: the coffered ceiling under the upper roof

throne dais._about: the throne's dais, its seven steps implied

lower beam._about: the painted beam round the column heads

lower brackets._about: bracket sets on every column and between them, under both eaves

lower roof._about: the lower roof: a ring of yellow glazed tile, its corners turned up, from the eave to the clerestory; ten beasts down each hip

clerestory._about: a band of lattice windows between the two roofs, to light the hall's high ceiling

upper roof._about: the upper roof, the true hip (wudian), the highest rank a Chinese roof could have: yellow tile, which only the emperor might use

ridge._about: the main ridge, and the chiwen -- the dragon-mouthed ridge ends, 3.4m tall

bronze vats._about: great gilded vats of water, for fires, along the terrace

zhonghe dian._about: the Hall of Central Harmony, 24m square, where the emperor rested on his way: a pyramid roof and a gilt ball

baohe dian._about: the Hall of Preserving Harmony, nine bays, its gablet roof a rank below the hip

axial way._about: the imperial way's flagstones running on south across the great court
